questionText: A certain processor deploys a single-level cache. The cache block size is 8 words and the word size is 4 bytes. The memory system uses a 60-MHz clock. To service a cache miss, the memory controller first takes 1 cycle to accept the starting address of the block, it then takes 3 cycles to fetch all the eight words of the block, and finally transmits the words of the requested block at the rate of 1 word per cycle. The maximum bandwidth for the memory system when the program running on the processor issues a series of read operations is ________ $\times 10^6$ bytes/sec.
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate total bytes transferred per block.
Block size = $8\text{ words}$
Word size = $4\text{ bytes}$
Total data per block = $8 \times 4 = 32\text{ bytes}$

Step 2: Calculate total clock cycles required for a cache miss.
1 cycle to accept the starting address
+ 3 cycles to fetch the 8 words
+ 8 cycles to transmit 8 words (at 1 word per cycle)
Total time taken in cycles = $1 + 3 + 8 = 12\text{ cycles}$

Step 3: Calculate the maximum memory bandwidth.
Clock frequency = $60 \text{ MHz} = 60 \times 10^6\text{ Hz}$
Bandwidth = $\frac{\text{Data transferred}}{\text{Cycles taken}} \times \text{Clock rate}$
Bandwidth = $\frac{32\text{ bytes}}{12\text{ cycles}} \times 60 \times 10^6\text{ cycles/sec} = 160 \times 10^6\text{ bytes/sec}$

Hence, the maximum bandwidth is 160 $\times 10^6\text{ bytes/sec}$.
